transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lena (CSM); Jenna (Infra), Raj (SRE), Tom (Security), Priya (ML)
Shared: security pack link (drive.redwood/example), benchmark csv placeholder

Summary: Quick sync on onboarding progress, credentials status, results from last week's bench, focused discussion on 99th pct latency and a light-weight rollback playbook for the POC. Agreed next steps around SSO metadata, KMS choices, and a follow-up bench run in their staging VPC.

Topics: onboarding creds, KMS/encryption, SSO test account, latency/99th tuning, KV cache behavior, rollback/playbook, artifacts to share.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining — i see most of the crew are on, we'll keep to 40 mins, quick check in. uh lena from cs is also here for handoff notes.
[00:18] Jenna (Infra): yep thanks, quick note — we fixed the routing rule for the staging gateway yesterday so creds provisioning should be unblocked, fingers crossed.
[00:29] Carlos (Redwood SE): nice, that should let us validate SAML and the temporary key access. Maya, you said security pack was basically ready?
[00:36] Maya (Redwood AE): yeah i'll drop a stripped down pack in the drive after the call, it has SOC2 excerpt, KMS patterns we support, and the audit-log outline. not the whole legal appendix, just the engineering bits.
[00:48] Tom (Security): great. question up front — do you support HSM-backed keys via our cloud KMS? we can't store plaintext keys in vendor-managed services.
[00:58] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via standard envelope encryption. there are two flow options: bring-your-own-key where the KMS signs tokens, or we call into your KMS for unwrap on dedicated/private. small note — there's a latency delta if you do synchronous unwrap on every request.
[01:21] Raj (SRE): that latency delta — is that like 10-ish ms per request? our 99th is already tight for chat flows.
[01:30] Carlos (Redwood SE): good question. depends on region and KMS, but synchronous unwrap can add 5–25ms per request in our experience. we usually recommend caching the decrypted envelope for the session where security policy allows — that reduces the impact to near-zero after first token. but that's a policy decision.
[01:49] Priya (ML Eng): for our use case we're doing short chat sessions 1–2 turns mostly, so the unwrap cost could be a significant fraction. is there a recommended compromise?
[02:00] Carlos (Redwood SE): for short sessions we suggest doing a short-lived session key: you unwrap once at session start and keep in kv-cache for the session TTL. that's safe if session TTL is small and we can log unwrap events to audit.
[02:13] Jenna (Infra): ok that sounds doable; we'll need the audit event schema though for our compliance folks.
[02:20] Maya (Redwood AE): i'll include the audit sample in the pack.
[02:25] Lena (CSM): quick check, are we tracking this as a blocker for go/no-go? or just a risk to document?
[02:32] Tom (Security): operationally it's a must-have for us to prove key custody. i wouldn't block the pilot but we need a clear playbook on where keys live and unwrap cadence.
[02:44] Maya (Redwood AE): noted. switching to lat bench results — carlos, can you summarize the numbers from last week's run?
[02:51] Carlos (Redwood SE): yeah so we ran the baseline against hosted Redwood model with quant profile Q4, burst concurrency 8, and their payload sample set. median token latency was 75ms, p95 ~ 310ms, p99 ~ 1.2s. the run indicated KV cache warmed after ~3 sessions which brought p99 down to ~650ms for repeated users. we observed a handful of outliers at 2.1s correlated with soft GC events on the node.
[03:21] Raj (SRE): 2.1s outliers are concerning — do you have traces? were those tabled to any particular model variant?
[03:30] Carlos (Redwood SE): traces linked in the csv, but quick answer: those were during a scheduled rotation on the node and we hit a path where the kernel fallback triggered a slower op. not model-specific but runtime event. on Dedicated you can avoid that by reserving nodes and disabling background compaction during POC windows.
[03:50] Priya (ML Eng): is there a tradeoff to disabling compaction? storage or memory impact?
[03:56] Carlos (Redwood SE): some memory fragmentation over long runs, but for a short POC run it's negligible. we can set compaction windows.
[04:04] Jenna (Infra): we want to retest in our staging VPC with peering — i can provision peering by tomorrow. question: will the Redwood bench script run from your side or ours?
[04:16] Carlos (Redwood SE): ideally we run a remote agent into your staging to generate realistic load, and you run a control bench from inside the VPC to compare. we can share the agent container (sha: redwood/bench:202608).
[04:30] Maya (Redwood AE): i'll add that container link in the notes.
[04:32] Tom (Security): another sec question — how does the KV cache handle PII? some of our prompts include PHI tokens; caching policy is a compliance risk.
[04:44] Carlos (Redwood SE): great callout. we support hashed-prefix-only caching and fine-grained cache controls per route. for PHI routes we recommend disabling caching or using deterministic masking on the prefix. Redwood also supports TTL=0 for cache bypass.
[04:59] Priya (ML Eng): masking might change model output distribution though — did you evaluate quality regressions if we mask names?
[05:06] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes there is slight quality delta, usually negligible for system prompts but noticeable if identity tokens are part of the prompt context. we can run a quick A/B eval with your test prompts to measure impact.
[05:18] Maya (Redwood AE): ok let's plan an A/B run in next bench.
[05:22] Lena (CSM): small process note — who owns the rollback playbook? customer or Redwood?
[05:28] Raj (SRE): i think we'll own ops playbook but we need Redwood input on safe fallback model variants and API-level toggles.
[05:36] Carlos (Redwood SE): we can provide a minimal rollback playbook with concrete commands: toggle route to lighter model, enable degraded mode (disable batch), route to hosted fallback, and revoke keys if needed. we'll provide command snippets for k8s and direct API toggles.
[05:54] Tom (Security): can you make those commands explicit? like curl toggles and example k8s patch? we prefer copy/paste.
[06:02] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes, we'll annotate with explicit curl samples and the RBAC step to rotate creds.
[06:09] Maya (Redwood AE): i'm noting that as an action for carlos and tom to collaborate.
[06:14] Jenna (Infra): on creds — our SAML metadata was modified; i'll send a test account today. prefer we use a test SSO user in the dev group.
[06:24] Raj (SRE): also forwarding network ACLs — there was an egress rule that blocked a small subset of IPs, might affect bench. i'll open a temporary allowlist with the bench agent IPs.
[06:33] Carlos (Redwood SE): perfect. once we have the staging VPC details we can kick a bench within their window.
[06:38] Priya (ML Eng): one more question on quality — we saw a small regression in RBI on summaries vs our golden set when the quant profile changed. what's the recommended way to test quant profiles in POC?
[06:48] Carlos (Redwood SE): run paired evals across quant profiles Q2/Q4/Q8 using the same prompts; we can automate this in the bench harness and output a diff report. for POC we recommend Q4 as balance; Q2 sometimes regresses some rare tokens.
[07:03] Maya (Redwood AE): will that be part of the next bench?
[07:06] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes we'll include Q2/Q4 pairs.
[07:10] Lena (CSM): ok we're at about 7 minutes in — sorry, timestamp confusing — actually 7 minutes? the recording shows more but okay. can we recap key blockers?
[07:19] Maya (Redwood AE): breakdown: 1) SSO/test account from Novara (customer) — blocker for SSO validation; 2) KMS decision and audit schema — customer action; 3) staging bench run inside peered VPC — Redwood action to run agent plus customer to open allowlist; 4) rollback playbook draft — Redwood to provide concrete commands and customer to review.
[07:44] Raj (SRE): yup that's accurate. Tom will own the compliance signoff.
[07:49] Tom (Security): correct, i'll synthesize a 1-page compliance checklist afterwards.
[07:55] Maya (Redwood AE): great — any other concerns with latency tail?
[08:01] Raj (SRE): curious about autoscaling thresholds — if we get to steady 200 RPS what do you recommend for concurrency?
[08:09] Carlos (Redwood SE): depends on model and dedicated vs hosted. for Q4-style the sweet spot was concurrency 8–12 per GPU for predictable 99th, but if you want lower p99 push concurrency down and scale instances horizontally. we'll share a cost/latency tradeoff table.
[08:26] Priya (ML Eng): does Redwood expose token-level billing in the POC so we can approximate cost per 1k users?
[08:33] Maya (Redwood AE): yes we expose token-level breakdowns in the console; for POC we can grant a 30-day view and a billing dashboard export.
[08:40] Jenna (Infra): ok that helps for our internal estimate.
[08:44] Lena (CSM): turning to operational alerts — can we set an alert on p99 > 1.5s?
[08:50] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes that's supported via our tracing integration, we can emit to pagerduty or to your metrics endpoint. we'll wire an example rule.
[08:59] Maya (Redwood AE): quick open item — competitors were asking about on-prem option; customer wants clarity on private deployment path but that's not in scope for this POC. should we note it?
[09:07] Tom (Security): we just want assurance we could move to private later if needed. not a blocker.
[09:12] Maya (Redwood AE): ok flagged as future scope.
[09:15] Carlos (Redwood SE): last technical note: when we run the new bench in their peered VPC i'll enable verbose tracing for a 30-minute window to capture KV hits and unwrap events, that should help tune cache TTLs.
[09:28] Raj (SRE): sounds good. please annotate which traces correspond to unwrap events so we can match to KMS logs.
[09:35] Carlos (Redwood SE): will do.
[09:37] Jenna (Infra): when can we expect the next touch after the bench?
[09:41] Maya (Redwood AE): i'll schedule a 30-min review the day after bench completes, likely Friday 2026-08-22.
[09:48] Priya (ML Eng): anything else on QA for masking vs caching?
[09:52] Carlos (Redwood SE): just that we'll include the masking A/B in the bench so we can quantify delta.
[09:58] Lena (CSM): great — last thing, can we get an exec one-pager for sponsors?
[10:03] Maya (Redwood AE): yes i'll produce a 1-pager summary with key metrics and risks.
[10:07] Tom (Security): thanks — that will help get compliance pre-approval.
[10:10] Maya (Redwood AE): ok wrapping: action items and next steps noted in drive. i'll send minutes. thanks everyone.
[10:18] (crosstalk, wrap)
[10:25] Speaker 1: bye all

End transcript.
